outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms appear likely late Friday afternoon and evening across parts of the western/central Dakotas, southeastern Montana, and northeastern Wyoming, accompanied by a risk for large hail and damaging wind gusts. Storms developing across the central High Plains and Southeast may also pose a risk for isolated damaging winds and hail.

sections.title: Northern Plains Vicinity
sections.text: A strong shortwave trough will track eastward across the northern Rockies today. This will bring a belt of 60-80 kt southwesterly midlevel flow across much of WY into eastern MT and the western Dakotas. At the surface, low-level moisture will stream northward on strong southerly 850mb wind and dewpoints will reach the upper 50s to low 60s from far eastern MT/northeast WY into the Dakotas. As temperatures aloft cool, lapse rates will increase and a corridor of weak to moderate buoyancy will develop by peak heating across parts of the northern High Plains. A surface trough will develop southward through the Dakotas and into the northern/central High Plains vicinity as a cold front shifts eastward across MT during the afternoon and into the Dakotas overnight. Thunderstorms are expected to develop during the afternoon in strong convergence along the surface boundary, and in increasing deep-layer ascent as the shortwave trough approaches, in the vicinity of the Big Horn mountains in northeast WY toward southeast MT and adjacent portions of the western Dakotas by late afternoon. sections.title: Southeastern U.S. Vicinity
sections.text: A very moist and moderately unstable airmass will reside across the southeastern U.S. as the Plains shortwave trough shifts eastward. Pockets of greater instability and lapse rates will coincide with modest deep-layer shear on the order of 25-35 kt and PW values around 1.5-2 inches. This could lead to a few strong wind gusts in better organized convection. Additionally, a corridor of stronger 0-3 km SRH greater than 150 m2/s2 will overspread parts of GA and the Carolinas as the remnants of the Gulf of Mexico subtropical low shifts east across the area. Given mean mixing ratios greater than 15 g/kg and modest low level shear in this area, a brief, weak tornado can not be ruled out.

sections.title: Central/Southern High Plains
sections.text: Isolated storms are expected during the afternoon and early evening along a weak surface trough and modest upslope flow. Strong heating and steep midlevel lapse rates will result in weak destabilization with MLCAPE has high as 1500 J/kg. Weak deep-layer shear will limit storm longevity/organization but a few stronger storms could produce marginal hail and gusty winds. ..Leitman/Dean.. 06/07/2019

outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms should produce severe hail and winds over a portion of the northern Plains this afternoon into evening.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, the split-flow pattern is forecast to shift eastward out of the central CONUS today and tonight, as progressive synoptic troughing proceeds eastward over the northern Rockies and Great Basin. The broad/weak cyclone responsible for the split flow -- initially centered over AR -- should move eastward across the Mid-South and Tennessee Valley regions through the period, while central height values fill slowly. By 12Z, the 500-mb cyclone center should be over western or middle TN, with trough southward across southeastern LA and the central Gulf. At the surface, a cold front associated with the northwestern upper trough was analyzed from a low near the northeast corner of MT, southwestward over northwestern WY to another low in the SLC area, then across east-central/southwestern NV and south-central CA. By 00Z, this front should extend from north-central/southwestern ND through a wave low over the eastern WY/MT state line, then southwestward across western WY to north-central UT and south- central NV. Lee troughing will extend from near that frontal wave across eastern portions of WY/CO/NM. By 12Z, the front should reach northeastern ND, west-central SD, southeaste

sections.title: Northern/central Plains
sections.text: Scattered thunderstorms are forecast to move northeastward across the northern Plains, offering severe gusts and occasional large hail. The most-concentrated severe potential, in terms of both supercellular hail threat in the earlier part of the convective cycle and wind throughout, still appears to be concentrated near and just southeast of the frontal zone, where low-level forcing will be relatively maximized. Foci for initiation of storms in this regime can be the front itself, along with the Beartooth, Absaroka and Bighorn Mountains, and the nearby portion of the lee trough over southeastern MT/northeastern WY and the northern Black Hills. Forecast vertical shear will favor early supercellular modes, with long low-level hodographs and effective-shear magnitudes around 40-50 kt. Large hail will be the most probable during that phase. With flow aloft strong but largely parallel to the frontal zone, convection in that area is expected to merge and evolve upscale. A forward-propagating, cold-pool-driven complex should develop, with the dominant threat becoming severe gusts northeastward through and near the remainder of the "enhanced" risk area. sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms, both discrete and clustered, are possible throughout the period, with peak coverage likely in the afternoon amidst greatest buoyancy. Isolated severe hail may occur over the western parts of the outlook area where deep-layer lapse rates will be greatest, while the severe-wind potential is more widely dispersed across the area (but still marginal overall). A tornado cannot be ruled out over portions of GA/Carolinas, mainly before late afternoon. In that area, relatively backed 850-mb winds, low-level hodographs and shear vectors will be maximized, east and southeast of a convectively aided midlevel vorticity lobe initially near the TN/AL border. A very moist air mass will be nearly ubiquitous over the outlook area, with PW 1.5-2 inches (locally higher), surface dew points commonly in the upper 60s and 70s F, and mean mixing ratios 15-18 g/kg. In tandem with pockets of strong surface heating, this will lead to swaths of 1500-2500 J/kg MLCAPE, with the greatest buoyancy in areas heated the longest. outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms should produce severe hail and winds over a portion of the northern Plains this afternoon into evening, while storms this afternoon could produce a few damaging gusts across parts of Alabama and Georgia.

sections.title: Northern High Plains this afternoon into tonight
sections.text: A pronounced mid-upper trough over the interior Pacific Northwest and northern Rockies will move slowly eastward toward the northern High Plains through early Saturday. An associated surface cold front will likewise move slowly east-southeastward across WY, eastern MT, and western ND, though progress of the front will be slowed some today by cyclogenesis in the lee of the Wind River Range in WY. Low-level moisture is modest across the northern High Plains this morning, with some increase possible across the Dakotas through weak advection and local evapotranspiration. However, the primary driver of buoyancy this afternoon will be surface heating/deep mixing near the lee cyclone/trough and along the cold front closer to the Big Horn Mountains. High-based thunderstorm development is expected by early-mid afternoon across northwest and north central WY as ascent downstream from an embedded speed max over the northern Great Basin interacts with the deepening boundary layer and at least weak surface-based buoyancy. Deep-layer vertical shear will favor supercells initially, with the potential to produce large hail and damaging winds. Eventual upscale growth into organized/bowing clusters

sections.title: Southeast states this afternoon/evening
sections.text: A midlevel low and weak surface reflection over AR as of late morning will only drift eastward through tonight. Surface heating within a very moist low-level air mass is contributing to moderate buoyancy in a corridor from southeast LA into AL/GA, in advance of ongoing/loosely organized storm clusters. Continued destabilization in conjunction with modest (roughly 30 kt) low-midlevel southwesterly flow will support a threat for expansion of the ongoing convection as a few multicell clusters capable of producing a few marginally severe outflow gusts with resultant wind damage. Along the northeast edge of the richer moisture and more unstable warm sector, there will be a zone of somewhat enhanced low-level shear/hodograph curvature across SC this afternoon. Here, weak supercell structures will be possible with an attendant threat for a brief tornado. However, the extent of the threat will be limited by rather modest low-level flow/SRH (effective SRH generally 150 m2/s2 or less) and deep-layer shear (effective bulk shear of 30 kt or less), in an environment with poor midlevel lapse rates. ..Thompson/Squitieri.. 06/07/2019

outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms should produce severe hail and winds over a portion of the northern Plains this afternoon and evening, while storms this afternoon should continue to produce a few damaging gusts across parts of the Southeast.

sections.title: 20Z Update
sections.text: The Slight risk has been expanded eastward across more of central/eastern GA to account for a strong to damaging wind threat associated with a small bowing cluster moving eastward around 40 kt. The airmass downstream of this convection has become moderately to strongly unstable, and around 30 kt of mid-level west-southwesterly flow should encourage continued storm organization through the early evening. No changes have been made to severe probabilities across the northern Plains. The risk for large hail and damaging winds is still expected to increase across this region later this afternoon into the evening. See Mesoscale Discussion 1016 for more information on the near-term severe threat across parts of western/central WY. ..Gleason.. 06/07/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1126 AM CDT Fri Jun 07 2019/

outlooks.summary: Damaging wind gusts and hail will be possible across portions of the northern Plains through late tonight. A few strong storms could also produce strong wind gusts across portions of the northern Gulf Coast vicinity.

sections.title: Northern Plains southwest to the southern High Plains
sections.text: Main adjustment across the northern Plains was to trim severe probabilities across north-central and northeast WY based on latest surface observations and where the cold front has already passed. Otherwise, the main body of the Slight and Enhanced risk areas remain relatively unchanged with only modest adjustments. Widely scattered severe thunderstorms have produced mainly large hail reports late this afternoon. As a low level jet increases during the next few hours, storms could still develop into a bowing segment tracking northeast across southwest and central ND. Further south, the Marginal risk has been trimmed across much of the central and southern High Plains as MLCIN quickly diminished the threat with southward extent into the remainder of the evening. A couple of thunderstorm clusters from the western NE Panhandle into northeast CO could still produce marginal hail or gusty winds in the short term however.

sections.title: Southeastern States
sections.text: The Slight risk has been removed with this update and the Marginal risk has been greatly reduced in aerial coverage. Where the Marginal remains (northern Gulf Coast into central AL/southwest GA), a band of stronger deep layer shear will persist overnight. This will help to maintain clusters of thunderstorms with an isolated threat for a downburst/locally strong gust in weak to moderate instability where PW values will remain in the 1.75-2.0 inch range. ..Leitman.. 06/08/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Bowing segment, capable of isolated damaging wind gusts, may continue for a few more hours. The sparse nature of the damaging wind threat suggests that a WW issuance is not likely at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A short convective bowing segment has developed across central MS over the past few hours. This segment is propagating eastward while traversing a modest low-level CAPE gradient, with a warming/deepening, moist boundary layer in place downstream. Latest HRRR guidance suggests that this convective cluster should persist eastward in some capacity into the late morning/early afternoon hours. Current mesoanalysis, and KGWX and KBMX VAD profiler data all depict a weak kinematic flow field in place, with less than 35 knots of bulk effective shear and around 50 m2/s2 of 0-3 km SRH. With regards to severe potential, pulsing cells embedded within the bowing segment are likely to become quickly undercut by the convective cold pool, which may hinder downward transport of higher momentum flow aloft. As the storms progress into a more heated airmass, some of the stronger cores may intensify briefly enough to allow water-loaded downdrafts to transport a few damaging gusts to the surface. Still, the sparse nature of the wind damage threat suggests that a WW issuance is not necessary at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Linear segments will continue to move eastward across the area during the early afternoon hours. Some of the stronger segments will be capable of producing damaging wind gusts. Convective trends will continue to be monitored for the possibility of a WW issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A relatively small but organized MCS continues to move eastward across central Alabama at around 40 knots. Ahead of the MCS, ample afternoon insolation has promoted a moderately buoyant airmass, with up to 2000 J/kg MLCAPE noted. Shear however, remains modest, with effective bulk shear values generally under 35 knots noted. As such, questions remain regarding how much further organization may occur with the MCS, particularly with regards to an organized damaging wind threat. Further heating/insolation may promote further intensification of a few cells embedded within the MCS, which in turn may produce at least a few severe gusts associated with water-loaded downdrafts amidst a very moist sfc-850 mb layer. However, the density of severe wind events warranting a WW issuance remains uncertain and as such, convective trends will continue to be monitored for possible further intensification and a subsequent need of a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few strong wind gusts are possible this afternoon across the central and southern High Plains.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Despite limited low-level moisture, ongoing deep boundary-layer mixing in the presence of steep mid-level lapse rates is resulting in air mass destabilization. This destabilizing environment has resulted in more robust convection over the past hour or so with a few storms now deep enough to produce lightning. Large-scale forcing for ascent will remain rather nebulous throughout the afternoon with most storms likely remaining over the higher terrain until they are deep enough for the southwesterly flow aloft to induce a more easterly storm motion off the terrain. A few storms may be able to move off the higher terrain, with an attendant threat for damaging downburst wind gusts as these high-based thunderstorms collapse over the lower elevations. Anticipated isolated and marginal nature of this threat will preclude watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms capable of strong wind gusts are possible over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent surface analysis shows a cold front extending from west-central WY northeastward to north-central WY and then back eastward into the far northeast portion of the state. A frontal low is centered about 30 miles east of RIW. Despite modest low-level moisture, air mass across much of WY ahead of this front continues to gradually destabilize amidst strong diurnal heating and deep boundary-layer mixing beneath steep mid-level lapse rates. Forcing for ascent along and ahead of the cold front, aided by increasing large-scale forcing for ascent ahead an approaching shortwave trough, within this destabilizing environment is expected to result in eventual convective initiation. Instability will remain rather limited, but moderate southwesterly mid- and upper-level flow will result in mean cloud-layer winds around 45-50 kt and the potential for occasional bowing segments capable of strong wind gusts. Limited severe coverage will likely preclude the need for a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Stronger storms may produce an isolated damaging wind gust or two. A brief tornado also cannot be ruled out. A WW issuance is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms continue to develop this afternoon as a small mid-level shortwave trough traverses the area, providing deep-layer ascent. Ample solar radiation/boundary layer heating is also contributing to both lift and destabilization, with up to 1500 J/kg MLCAPE noted. A few transient supercell structures have been noted immediately northeast of CAE within the past hour, likely due to slightly enhanced low-level shear present along a diffuse baroclinic zone, roughly paralleling the SC/NC border. While the CAE VAD profiler depicts a curved hodograph in the lowest 1 km, the weak magnitudes of the winds aloft (and thus the small size of the hodographs), suggest that any organized updrafts that becomes sustained will likely acquire brief periods of low-level rotation at best. Such storms will be capable of producing a couple damaging wind gusts, and a brief tornado also cannot be ruled out. Given the short duration and spatially sparse nature of the severe threat, a WW issuance is not anticipated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Gradually increasing thunderstorm coverage is anticipated. Some of these storms could produce strong wind gusts.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 20Z surface analysis places a cold front from central ND southwestward into northwest SD and then westward into north-central WY. Air mass ahead of this front across the Dakotas has remained capped while only minimal convective inhibition remains across much of WY. Portion of this front across WY and western SD is expected to slow its forward progression while the northern portion remains more progressive. Expectation is for thunderstorm coverage and strength to gradually increase across central WY as ascent attendant to the shortwave trough moving through UT/ID moves eastward. This activity is then expected to move northeastward, with the front augmenting lift and strengthening ongoing cells. Increasing southwesterly flow aloft will result in fast storm motion while the deeply mixed boundary layer supports strong cold pool development. Trends are being monitored across this region for evidence of this convective evolution and resulting potential for a watch. Farther south (across southeast WY/western NE Panhandle), a cluster of cold pool dominated thunderstorms is moving northeastward. Deeply mixed boundary layer downstream may promote occasionally strong wind gusts. There is a low probability this cluster evolves into a more organized convective system.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few more damaging wind gusts may occur with eastward moving cluster of storms over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An MCS continues to progress eastward across central GA, amidst an ambient environment characterized by 2000 J/kg MLCAPE and effective bulk shear values around 30-35 knots. Until the onset of nocturnal cooling, the MCS will likely maintain some momentum, with a few of the more intense/organized embedded cells capable of producing water-loaded downdrafts and subsequent damaging wind gusts. It is possible that organized convection, perhaps with a sparse wind threat, may expand just east of the Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0339 bounds.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm clusters will continue to pose a threat of locally damaging wind into the early evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several thunderstorm clusters are ongoing at 2130Z across eastern MS, with activity beginning to move into western AL. The thermodynamic environment across the region is characterized by generally weak midlevel lapse rates, but also rich low-level moisture and temperatures warming to near 90F downstream of ongoing storms, supporting MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg. Area VWPs suggest the strongest shear (effective shear of 30-40 kt) is located across the southern half of the MCD area, within a region of moderate midlevel westerly flow to the southeast of a well-defined upper trough to the northwest. Storms across southeast MS into southwest AL may display supercell characteristics at times, with a threat of locally damaging wind and some (generally subsevere) hail. Across the northern portion of the MCD area, shear is somewhat weaker, but instability is more than sufficient to support strong convection, and ongoing cumulus development across west-central/northwest AL suggests upstream clusters should persist into this area, with a corresponding threat of locally damaging wind associated with any upscale growing segments. While some sporadic damaging wind is possible across portions of the MCD area, at this time the overall threat appears too limited in coverage/intensity for watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe risk is beginning to ramp up for areas over northwest SD and southwest ND. Severe gusts (60-75mph) and large hail (1-2 inches in diameter) are the threats with the stronger storms.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Water-vapor imagery shows a potent mid-level shortwave trough moving through the Northern Rockies and northern InterMountain regions early this evening. Farther east over the western Dakotas and southeast MT, the initial plume of 700-500mb ascent will overspread this area during the next 1-2 hours according to objective analyses. Surface analysis via observations and radar fine-line data indicate a cold front is slowly pushing east across central ND with the boundary stalling near the Black Hills. Surface dewpoints in the middle 50s are located over southwest ND into northwest SD. It appears most of the ongoing thunderstorm activity moving into the western Dakotas is preferentially favoring the cool-side of the boundary where shallow frontal lift is more supportive for storm development compared to a capped warm sector farther east. Some short-term convection-allowing model guidance is suggestive that the ongoing storms over southeast MT and the area along the SD/WY border is the initial evolution of a severe-wind producing cluster of thunderstorms expected to move northeast across southwest ND/northwest SD and eventually into central ND later this evening. A new severe thunderstorm watch will likely be needed farther northeast of severe thunderstorm watch 340. However, during the next 1-2 hours, the expectation is for a gradual intensification of storms over southeast MT moving into the western Dakotas with the risk for severe gusts coincidentally increasing. ..Smith.. 06/07/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of large hail and severe wind gusts will continue, with some upscale growth possible later this evening into northwest SD/southwest ND.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Two long-lived elevated clusters are moving across the northern portion of WW 340 as of 0045Z, with another outflow-driven cluster moving northeastward out of the Black Hills. The northern clusters are likely somewhat elevated and are moving along the northern edge of stronger MUCAPE (1000-2000 J/kg per recent mesoanalyses). Effective shear of 35-45 kt (for parcels originating around 800 mb) is more than sufficient to maintain organized structures through the evening. As convection evolves tonight, one or more upscale growing clusters may develop, either as separate clusters begin to consolidate, or as bowing segments develop out of the existing clusters. The northern clusters have shown some tendency toward a more linear mode over the last half hour, as new updrafts preferentially develop on the south edge closer to the stronger buoyancy. Should upscale growth occur, an increasing severe wind threat will spread downstream into the northeastern portion of WW 340 and the southwest portion of newly issued WW 341. Otherwise, existing activity will continue to pose a threat of hail and localized severe wind through the evening. ..Dean.. 06/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe gusts remain possible for the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a cluster of thunderstorms paralleling a surface front near the SD/ND border and moving northeast. The terminus of a strong 50kt southerly LLJ and near 8 degrees C/km 700-500mb lapse rates will act to sustain the thunderstorms for the next few hours. Although convective inhibition is increasing, the steep 700-500mb lapse rates provide some potential for intermittently invigorated downdrafts capable of isolated severe gusts (60mph). ..Smith.. 06/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
